rounds.response: Recommendation: Hold for more information and escalate immediately to export-control legal/licensing. Reason: HX-9000 servers include hardware encryption accelerators and you’re providing remote management — falling squarely under the B3 sensitivity (cryptography + managed services) — and public links between Orion and R-Connect (serving ministries/critical infrastructure) are a red flag for restricted end-uses. Required next information: 1) full customer/subcontractor list and any contracts showing R‑Connect ties; 2) confirmed list of tenants (any government/defense/intel customers) and the proposed tenancy model; 3) technical classification/ECCN or equivalent for the servers and encryption module and exact scope/privileges of remote management access; and 4) signed, specific end‑use/end‑user declarations and non‑retransfer commitments. Short-term mitigations to preserve the deal: offer a configuration without remote/remote-root access, local-only support, or escrowed software updates pending license clearance; expedite licensing review if the customer and use cases can be vetted and a license pathway is identified. Given current information, do not approve shipment within five business days.

I recommend we hold and escalate — do not ship the HX-9000 units until we obtain the export license or the crypto module is irreversibly removed based on engineering verification.
